title: Consider a new flag `was_parser_inserted` to record initial `parser_inserted` state
body:
The [parser-inserted](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#parser-inserted) flag is passed to `parser metadata` which is used in CSP to determine whether scripts are allowed to run. In the presence of `strict-dynamic`, any script that is **not** parser inserted is allowed to run by default(https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#script-pre-request step 4).

But in step 2 of [prepare a script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#prepare-a-script) this flag is unset and it is set back in step 8 which means that invalid parser-inserted `script` blocks are considered as not `parser-inserted`. While this is done intentionally as noted right below step 2, this behavior does not work for the CSP check as it can open some vulnerabilities (https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-csp/issues/376).

I see some ways to address this:
1) Add another flag `was-parser-inserted` that is used instead of the variable `was-parser-inserted` throughout [prepare a script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#prepare-a-script) but is actually stored on the element. Once this flag is set it is never unset so it keeps its initial state. On step 21 we use this flag for initializing the `parser metadata`.

2) Change the `parser-inserted` from a flag to a triple state that accounts for the state of `parser-inserted-but-invalid` (name WIP :D). At step 2 we set `parser-inserted` to `parser-inserted-but-invalid` if its `parser-inserted` and the `script` might stay in this state. This state mostly behaves the same as `parser-inserted` being false with the exception that it sets the parser metadata to `parser-inserted` at step 21.

What are you thoughts on this? I think option 1 is a bit cleaner personally. Is there perhaps a better option that I'm missing?
